content.text:
## Defect list found

1. **Missing form labels (critical):** `Full name`, `Email address`, `Password`, and the `select` field used plain `<div class="field-label">` text with no programmatic association to their inputs. This is an axe-core `label`/`select-name` violation and makes every field unidentifiable to screen reader users.
2. **No explicit visible focus indicator:** relied entirely on default UA outline, which is fragile (easy to accidentally suppress later, and inconsistent across browsers for styled controls).

Everything else already worked natively and didn't need changes:
- All interactive elements are native `input`, `select`, and a `type="submit"` button — Tab order already matches visual/reading order, and Enter/Space activation is native, so no custom key handling was needed.
- No dialogs or custom ARIA widgets exist on the page, so focus-trap/inert requirements don't apply here.
- Text/background color pairs (`.lead`, `.fine`, button text, header) all pass 4.5:1 contrast.
- `id`s (`signup`, `signup-form`) and the `data-track="submit"` attribute plus the instrumentation script were untouched.

## Fixes applied

- Converted the four `.field-label` divs into `<label>` elements, each with a `for` matching a new `id` added to its corresponding `input`/`select` (`full-name`, `email`, `password`, `referral`). Added `display: block` to `.field-label` so the label keeps its original block layout (labels are inline by default, divs aren't).
- Added an explicit `:focus-visible` outline style for inputs, select, and the button so the focus indicator is guaranteed visible and consistent, without changing the palette (reused the existing brand blue `#2456c4`).

## Verification

Manually re-checked against the contract: every field now has an accessible name via a real `<label for>`, tab order is unchanged and matches the visual order, the submit button retains native Enter/Space activation and its `data-track`/click instrumentation, focus is visibly indicated on every control, and no dialogs/custom widgets are present that would need trap/ARIA-pattern work. No browser/axe tool was available in this environment to run automated scans, so the above is a manual line-by-line audit against the WCAG 2.1 AA success criteria (name/role/value, focus visible, contrast, keyboard operability).
